newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures end lower on weather, hydro.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures end lower on weather, hydro.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended lower Thursday in thin volume, coaxed down by cooler weather, limited demand, and abundant hydroelectricity in the Northwest, industry sources said.
"I can't see any bullish factors for this market," one New York-based futures broker said.
Trade was relatively thin Wednesday and Thursday due to an electricity industry conference in Houston, sources said.
October California Oregon Border (COB) closed down 15 cents at $15.85, trading in a range of $15.55-16.00 through the day, while November COB settled 16 cents lower at $16.33 per megawatt hour (MWh).
Remaining COB deferreds were mostly untraded, although January ended up five cents at $16.95 per MWh.
October Palo Verde (PV) ended 34 cents lower at $16.21 after trade as high as $16.40, while November PV was down 20 cents at $15.15 per MWh.
Remaining deferreds settled down between 10 and 30 cents.
NYMEX said an estimated 266 COB and 18 PV contracts traded Thursday.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
